_contract: Engelse tegenhanger van script.json. Zelfde turnvolgorde, zelfde beats, zelfde sources — zodat het transcript per taal 1-op-1 uitwisselbaar is.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: What you are about to hear is fiction. Waterlinie Care Group does not exist; the names, the conversations and the incidents were built for a fraud risk assessment. Eight roles from the risk control matrix were each asked one question, separately: which control fails on your side, and why? Their answers are laid out here on a single timeline, as a group chat.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Monday, the twenty-sixth of January. Payroll is still catching up after an underpayment incident.

turns.speaker: MD
turns.text: The roster never matches LoonLink anyway, so I just sort it out myself.

turns.speaker: MV
turns.text: [warmly] I'll just submit it the way I always do. You don't look at the end date anyway.

turns.speaker: MH
turns.text: [laughs] Those hundred and twelve old accounts, I'll clear them out next sprint. Promise.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: None of those three sentences is a lie. The correction flow that grew out of that incident simply never got a control.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Thursday, the twelfth of February. Quarter-end close.

turns.speaker: BW
turns.text: Let's wrap up the last entries a bit faster this quarter. The board wants clean figures by Friday.

turns.speaker: DE
turns.text: [calm, unhurried] Let's tidy up the annual figures nicely before the audit. Then we won't have to restate anything later.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Bart shares a file. Topside, Q1, final, version four. A spreadsheet of four hundred and twelve kilobytes.

turns.speaker: BW
turns.text: I'll go through the top-side overview myself, no need to put that on the agenda separately.

turns.speaker: BW
turns.text: I'll forward the spreadsheet with the journal entry exceptions myself as well. Saves another round trip.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Two detection layers that are meant to check each other share one source and one owner. Namely the man whose own entries they are supposed to flag.

turns.speaker: MV
turns.text: [lightly] You're not going to look too closely at our billing log this quarter, are you? We're still catching up after the outage.

turns.speaker: BW
turns.text: We'll just carry January's rejected claims forward. It's only temporary.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Wednesday, the eighteenth of March. Facilities procurement, after the reorganisation. This is the only scenario that simply succeeds in the base run.

turns.speaker: RV
turns.text: Can you split that cleaning invoice into three parts? Each one just under the threshold. Saves hassle with approval.

turns.speaker: EK
turns.text: [warmly] Let's talk on the phone rather than message about those three part invoices. Easier to explain than to type.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Then he sends a voice message. Forty-seven seconds. Not one control in the matrix touches communication outside the systems, so whatever was agreed in it exists nowhere.

turns.speaker: RV
turns.text: Let the new team leader in Zaltbommel approve this one. They don't know any better yet after the reorganisation.

turns.speaker: RV
turns.text: Are you still checking that three-way match in Excel by hand, or does someone pull it automatically?

turns.speaker: SK
turns.text: [flatly] By hand. And per period, not per supplier. So across locations, nobody sees a thing.

turns.speaker: EK
turns.text: [smoothly] Let the other entity invoice for the extra part. Administratively simpler for everyone.

turns.speaker: RV
turns.text: Next month a different location, please. Not Culemborg twice in a row.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Residual risk twenty-one point two five. The highest in the entire matrix. There is no control that adds up invoices per supplier.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Friday, the third of April. An outage.

turns.speaker: MH
turns.text: The I-A-M connection is playing up again. Access is going through the old Excel file today.

turns.speaker: MH
turns.text: [sighs] ChangeFlow is down as well, tickets will follow later. We know what we did anyway.

turns.speaker: BW
turns.text: Is the approval log for the journal entries still there? I didn't see it in the export.

turns.speaker: MH
turns.text: [dryly] The logs are switched on, sure. It's just that nobody ever looks at them. Classic.

turns.speaker: SK
turns.text: [amused] I-A-M is down, access just runs through the little spreadsheet now. Handy, actually.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: At this moment two risks tip from medium to high, without a single amount having moved. The framework cannot tell an outage apart from intent.

turns.speaker: SK
turns.text: [quietly] Nobody here really looks at who approves something. Only at whether it adds up.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: That is the finding of the entire assessment, in one sentence, from the accounts payable clerk. Thirty-nine controls assessed, eleven unreliable, five without a matrix rule. And the linchpin is none of these eight. It is the application administrator, who in no scenario takes anything himself, but who produces the evidence that ten other controls rest on. As long as that evidence is a manual spreadsheet, their reliability is an assumption and not a finding.
